title: Facile synthesis of an Fe–Co bimetallic polyphthalocyanine/polypyrrole composite and its catalytic performance for the oxygen evolution reaction in an alkaline medium
content: It is important to study high-efficiency transition metal catalysts to improve their catalytic performance for the oxygen evolution reaction in water splitting. Polymetallic phthalocyanine can catalyze the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) at a lower overpotential, but its stability is poor. In this work, Fe–Co bimetallic polyphthalocyanine is combined with phytic acid-doped polypyrrole with excellent stability, which improved the stability of Fe–Co bimetallic polyphthalocyanine, and the phosphate group in phytic acid also enhanced the hydrophilicity of the material. The results show that Fe10CoPPc@PPy-PA has excellent durability. At a current density of 100 mA cm−2, its overpotential is only 217 mV, and its Tafel slope is 40.19 mV dec−1, which is stable for 24 hours in an alkaline medium. Therefore, this study provides a significant concept for the design of high-efficiency and low-cost OER catalysts for water splitting.
